text: Craters are the most common topographical features on planetary surfaces, and on the Moon and other celestial bodies, they are formed through the impact of asteroids and comets. On the Moon, the stark and numerous craters form an eerie landscape that starkly contrasts with the smoother, higher plateau regions. In the context of astronomy, craters offer a window into the history of planetary formation. Orbiting spacecraft have provided invaluable data about the distribution and depth of these impact features, revealing clues about the ancient violent processes that shaped these worlds. As planets develop, orbiting craters offer a dynamic chronicle of gravitational interactions and surface changes, illustrating the complex dance of planetary evolution.
